items.title: [Bug]: step3 streaming tool parser returns empty arguments unless each token arrives in its own delta
items.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```text
Pure-Python logic bug in vllm/tool_parsers/step3_tool_parser.py.
Reproducible on current main (e47356c63) on any hardware, CPU only, no GPU needed.
Flags: --tool-call-parser step3
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `--tool-call-parser step3`, a streamed tool call carries the correct function
name but **empty arguments** unless every token happens to arrive in its own delta.
Non-streaming is unaffected.

Replaying the parser's own test sample (65 tokens) and cutting it into two deltas at
each of the 64 possible boundaries:

```
1 token per delta      : [('get_weather', '{"city": "Tokyo"}')]
2 deltas, split after 1: [('get_weather', '')]
whole stream, 1 delta  : [('get_weather', '')]

27 of 64 two-delta splits differ from the per-token baseline,
and all 27 return a tool call with empty arguments.
Failing split points: 1..27 (contiguous).
```

A client receives a syntactically valid tool call whose arguments are gone, with
HTTP 200 and no error. Multi-token deltas are the normal case in production:
`--stream-interval > 1`, speculative decoding, and ordinary scheduler batching all
produce them.

#### Cause

In `extract_tool_calls_streaming`, the branch that first parses the function name
returns immediately:

```python
# Send the function name as soon as it's parsed.
if not self.current_tool_name_sent:
    self.current_tool_name_sent = True
    self.prev_tool_call_arr[self.current_tool_id].update(tool_call_arr)
    return DeltaMessage(tool_calls=[DeltaToolCall(..., function=DeltaFunctionCall(name=function_name))])
```

That `return` exits the processing loop without advancing `self.position` past the
tool body. Arguments are only emitted further down, in the `if end_tool_pos != -1:`
branch, which therefore requires a **subsequent** call to
`extract_tool_calls_streaming`.

When the invoke tag, the parameters and `<｜tool_call_end｜>` all arrive in the same
delta, the name is sent and the call returns; there is no later delta, so the
arguments branch never runs and the arguments are lost.

This explains the contiguous failing range exactly. The prefix through token 27 is:

```
<｜tool_calls_begin｜><｜tool_call_begin｜><steptml:invoke name="get_weather"><
```

For a split at token ≤ 27 the first delta does not yet contain a complete
`<steptml:invoke name="...">`, so the name is first parsed in the second delta,
which also carries the end token, and the arguments are dropped. For a split at
token ≥ 28 the name is sent on the first delta and the second delta reaches the
`end_tool_pos != -1` branch normally.

#### Reproduction

Self-contained, uses only the public parser API:

```python
from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
from vllm.tokenizers import get_tokenizer
from vllm.tool_parsers import ToolParserManager

OUTPUT = (
    "<｜tool_calls_begin｜><｜tool_call_begin｜>"
    '<steptml:invoke name="get_weather">'
    '<steptml:parameter name="city">Tokyo</steptml:parameter>'
    "</steptml:invoke>"
    "<｜tool_call_end｜><｜tool_calls_end｜>"
)

tok = get_tokenizer("stepfun-ai/step3")
req = ChatCompletionRequest(messages=[], model="test")
ids = tok.encode(OUTPUT, add_special_tokens=False)
texts, prev = [], ""
for i in range(1, len(ids) + 1):
    cur = tok.decode(ids[:i])
    texts.append(cur[len(prev):])
    prev = cur


def stream(batches):
    p = ToolParserManager.get_tool_parser("step3")(tok)
    pt, pi, calls = "", [], {}
    for s, e in batches:
        dt = "".join(texts[s:e]); di = ids[s:e]
        ct, ci = pt + dt, pi + di
        m = p.extract_tool_calls_streaming(pt, ct, dt, pi, ci, di, req)
        if m is not None:
            for tc in (m.tool_calls or []):
                d = calls.setdefault(tc.index, {"name": "", "args": ""})
                if tc.function.name:
                    d["name"] = tc.function.name
                if tc.function.arguments:
                    d["args"] += tc.function.arguments
        pt, pi = ct, ci
    return [(v["name"], v["args"]) for v in calls.values()]


n = len(ids)
print("1 token per delta      :", stream([(i, i + 1) for i in range(n)]))
print("2 deltas, split after 1:", stream([(0, 1), (1, n)]))
print("whole stream, 1 delta  :", stream([(0, n)]))

base = stream([(i, i + 1) for i in range(n)])
bad = [i for i in range(1, n) if stream([(0, i), (i, n)]) != base]
print(f"{len(bad)}/{n - 1} two-delta splits differ: {bad}")
```

#### Notes

- Open PR #49567 touches this file (whitespace in parameter values). I applied it and
  re-ran the scan above: the result is unchanged, 27/64, so it does not address this.
- `tests/tool_parsers/test_step3_tool_parser.py` already carries `xfail_streaming`
  entries noting the parser has bugs, but none describes this boundary dependence.
- This is the same class as #48020 and #48342 (deepseek_v3), #47907 (granite,
  granite-20b-fc, gigachat3), #48294 (llama3_json, jamba, ernie45) and #48347
  (internlm): the streamed result depends on how tokens are batched into deltas.
  The general property test that surfaces it is proposed in #55079, where step3 is
  currently marked `xfail`.
- A Rust step3 tool parser is in flight in #46369; worth checking it against the same
  scan before it lands.

### Before submitting a new issue...

items.title: [Feature]: Tokenized Prompt as Input for Chat and Messages Endpoints when serving
items.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

# Feature Request: Tokenized Prompt Input for Chat and Messages Endpoints

## Summary

It would be useful for vLLM HTTP serving endpoints such as `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages` to accept prompt token IDs as input and skip repeated tokenization, while still preserving normal handling for tools, reasoning, and multimodal content.

The concrete examples below focus on `/v1/chat/completions`, but the same need also applies to agent-style message APIs.

This is related to the earlier feature request in [vLLM issue #25051](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/25051) (Stale, closed, and maybe outdated).

## Motivation

The main goal is simple: if a frontend already has prompt token IDs, vLLM's HTTP chat/message endpoint should be able to consume those IDs directly and skip tokenization.

For example, an HTTP routing layer such as vLLM Router may tokenize requests before forwarding them to workers so it can reuse repeated prompt prefixes, estimate prefill cost, or make cache-aware scheduling decisions. If `/v1/chat/completions` cannot accept those token IDs, vLLM has to apply the chat template and tokenize again.

Current flow:

```text
Client chat request
  -> HTTP frontend/router
  -> apply chat template + tokenize for cache/scheduling
  -> vLLM HTTP API server
  -> apply chat template + tokenize again
  -> engine
```

Desired flow:

```text
Client chat request
  -> HTTP frontend/router
  -> apply chat template + tokenize once
  -> vLLM HTTP API server accepts prompt token IDs
  -> skip tokenization, preserve chat/tool/multimodal handling
  -> engine
```

For pure completion-style requests, vLLM already supports this pattern. `/v1/completions` can accept token IDs through the `prompt` field:

```json
{
  "model": "model-name",
  "prompt": [151644, 872, 198, 9906],
  "max_tokens": 64
}
```

Offline and lower-level generation paths also support token-ID-style inputs. Internally, tokenized multimodal inputs are represented as token IDs plus separate multimodal payload fields, not as token IDs alone.

For chat-style endpoints, however, users currently cannot cleanly provide the already-tokenized chat prompt through the OpenAI-compatible HTTP API. This blocks tokenization-cache reuse at the HTTP frontend layer and can cause duplicate work:

1. A frontend applies the chat template and tokenizes the prompt for tokenization-cache reuse or scheduling/cache logic.
2. vLLM receives the original chat request and applies the chat template/tokenizes again.

Using `/v1/completions` as a workaround is not equivalent, because chat-completion-specific logic can be missed, especially tool call handling, reasoning parser adjustments, and multimodal processing.

## Requested Behavior

Add a supported tokenized-input path for `/v1/chat/completions`, and ideally a similar shape for `/v1/messages`.

The key requirement is that this should not be interpreted as "token IDs are the whole request." For chat and multimodal workloads, token IDs only represent the text/token sequence. Other request semantics still need to be preserved or passed separately.

A safe design should support:

- pre-tokenized prompt IDs for the final model prompt
- normal chat metadata such as `messages`, `tools`, `tool_choice`, and chat options
- multimodal payload data separately from token IDs
- multimodal processor kwargs / UUIDs where applicable
- normal reasoning/tool parser adjustments
- normal response formatting and usage accounting

For text-only chat, one possible shape is:

```json
{
  "model": "model-name",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}
  ],
  "prompt_token_ids": [151644, 872, 198, 9707, 151645, 198],
  "max_tokens": 64
}
```

For multimodal chat, token IDs alone are not sufficient. The API should either keep the original multimodal `messages` so vLLM can extract/process multimodal data normally, or expose an explicit tokenized prompt object similar to vLLM's internal/offline representation:

```json
{
  "model": "model-name",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."},
        {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://example.com/image.png"}}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "prompt_token_ids": [151644, 872, 198, 1234, 5678, 151645, 198],
  "mm_processor_kwargs": {},
  "max_tokens": 64
}
```

Conceptually, this matches the internal idea of:

```python
TokensPrompt(
    prompt_token_ids=[...],
    multi_modal_data={...},
    mm_processor_kwargs={...},
    multi_modal_uuids={...},
)
```

The exact public HTTP shape does not need to be identical to the internal Python type. The important part is that multimodal data and multimodal processor metadata remain separate from `prompt_token_ids`.

## Proposed Semantics

When tokenized prompt input is provided:

- vLLM should use the supplied prompt token IDs as the final text tokenization result.
- vLLM should skip the final tokenizer encode call for the rendered chat prompt.
- vLLM should still validate/process the original chat request enough to preserve tools, reasoning, multimodal data extraction, and response behavior.
- For multimodal requests, vLLM should still build the correct multimodal engine input from the multimodal payload and the supplied token IDs.
- If supplied token IDs do not match the expected multimodal placeholder layout, vLLM should return a clear validation error rather than silently producing inconsistent engine input.

## Why `prompt_token_ids` Alone May Not Be Enough

A single optional `prompt_token_ids` field can be enough for text-only chat if the original `messages` and tool fields are still present and vLLM continues to run the normal chat-processing path.

It is not enough as a standalone replacement for the whole chat request. Token IDs do not carry:

- image/audio/video payloads
- multimodal UUID/cache metadata
- multimodal processor kwargs
- tool schemas and tool-choice semantics
- message roles and response-format context
- reasoning/tool parser context

So the feature should be documented as "pre-tokenized prompt plus normal chat/multimodal metadata," not "send only token IDs."

## Possible Implementation Direction

One possible approach for `/v1/chat/completions`:

```python
class ChatCompletionRequest(OpenAIBaseModel):
    messages: list[ChatCompletionMessageParam]
    model: str | None = None

    # vLLM extension for the final rendered prompt token IDs.
    prompt_token_ids: list[int] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Pre-tokenized final chat prompt IDs. When provided, vLLM uses "
            "these IDs as the prompt tokenization result while preserving "
            "normal chat processing for tools, reasoning, and multimodal data."
        ),
    )
```

And in the render path:

```python
if request.prompt_token_ids is not None:
    if len(request.prompt_token_ids) == 0:
        return error("prompt_token_ids must not be empty")

    # Still run normal chat rendering/validation enough to preserve semantics
    # not represented by token IDs: tool-call state, multimodal payload
    # extraction, optional prompt text, etc.
    conversation, prompt = await renderer.render_messages_async(
        request.messages,
        chat_params,
    )

    # Replace only the text tokenization result.
    prompt = dict(prompt)
    prompt["prompt_token_ids"] = list(request.prompt_token_ids)
    prompt.pop("prompt", None)

    # Continue normal tool/reasoning adjustment and multimodal processing.
    tok_prompt = await renderer.tokenize_prompt_async(prompt, tok_params)
    engine_input = await renderer.process_for_engine_async(tok_prompt, ...)
    return conversation, [engine_input]
```

This is only a code sketch. The exact implementation should be checked carefully against vLLM's current chat render path, multimodal processor, and tool parser internals.

## Correctness Requirements

The feature should be considered correct only if these cases continue to work:

- text-only chat request with supplied prompt token IDs
- chat request with tools/tool choice
- chat request with reasoning parser behavior
- multimodal chat request where image/audio/video data is still processed correctly
- validation failure when token IDs are inconsistent with required multimodal placeholders
- streaming and non-streaming responses
- usage accounting based on supplied prompt token IDs

## Expected Benefit

This would expose a clean HTTP-level path for advanced serving systems that already compute token IDs before sending requests to vLLM. It would avoid duplicate chat-template/tokenization work while preserving the correctness of chat, tools, reasoning, and multimodal behavior.

It would also make chat/message-style HTTP endpoints more consistent with existing token-ID support in `/v1/completions` and offline/lower-level generation APIs.

> **Edited.** The original body claimed that `--reasoning-parser qwen3` leaves
> `reasoning_content` empty. That was wrong — it works, and it is a usable
> workaround. The section is corrected in place below; the retraction and the
> evidence are in the comments, which is why they refer to text no longer here.

### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```
vLLM version : 0.26.0 (from GET /version)
Model        : Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B  (stock, apache-2.0; config model_type=qwen3_5)

PyTorch      : 2.11.0+cu129 (CUDA 12.9)
Python       : 3.12.12
OS           : Linux 5.15.0 (x86_64, glibc 2.31)
```

</details>

Server command (note: **no `--reasoning-parser`**):

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml \
    --port 8020 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --mamba-cache-mode align \
    --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --disable-custom-all-reduce \
    --enforce-eager
```

> One deviation, in the interest of a repro anyone can run: our server was
> actually started with an additional `--chat-template <custom>.jinja`. For the
> single-user-message prompt used below that file renders **byte-identically** to
> the checkpoint's built-in `chat_template.jinja` (both verified through Jinja
> directly), so the flag is dropped here as it is not part of the mechanism. We
> have not re-run the repro with the built-in template selected explicitly.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `--tool-call-parser qwen3_xml` and **no reasoning parser configured**, the
`</think>` tag is consumed by the parser and never reaches the client. Because
no reasoning parser is configured there is also no `reasoning_content` field to
receive the reasoning — so the reasoning text is silently concatenated into
`content` ahead of the answer, with the only boundary marker removed. A chat
client is left with no way to tell deliberation from the final answer.

The Qwen3 chat template opens `<think>\n` in the generation prompt, so every
reply begins inside a think block and the model closes it with `</think>` before
answering. That closing tag is the client's only signal, and it is exactly what
goes missing.

**A workaround exists** — attach `--reasoning-parser qwen3` and the split is
correct (see below). The report is that the asymmetric configuration loses
information *silently*, not that there is no way to avoid it.

#### Reproduction

Send the same prompt two ways — through `/v1/chat/completions` (template renders
the prompt, output passes the tool-call parser) and through `/v1/completions`
(identical prompt string, no parser). The rendered generation prompt is
byte-identical in both cases:

```
'<|im_start|>user\nWhat is 17*23?<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n'
```

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
import json, urllib.request

BASE, MODEL = "http://127.0.0.1:8020", "Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B"
PROMPT = "What is 17*23?"
# Exactly what the model's own chat template renders for the message list below
# (verified with AutoTokenizer.apply_chat_template(..., add_generation_prompt=True)).
RAW = f"<|im_start|>user\n{PROMPT}<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n"

def post(path, payload):
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + path, data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600) as fh:
        return json.load(fh)

for i in range(5):
    d = post("/v1/chat/completions", {"model": MODEL, "max_tokens": 1500, "temperature": 0.7,
                                      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": PROMPT}]})
    m = d["choices"][0]["message"]
    t = m.get("content") or ""
    print(f"A chat/completions  close_tag={'</think>' in t!s:<5} len={len(t):<5} "
          f"reasoning_content={m.get('reasoning_content')!r}")

for i in range(5):
    d = post("/v1/completions", {"model": MODEL, "prompt": RAW,
                                 "max_tokens": 1500, "temperature": 0.7})
    t = d["choices"][0]["text"]
    print(f"B completions       close_tag={'</think>' in t!s:<5} len={len(t):<5}")
```

</details>

Output:

```
A chat/completions  close_tag=False len=848   reasoning_content=None
A chat/completions  close_tag=False len=832   reasoning_content=None
A chat/completions  close_tag=False len=905   reasoning_content=None
A chat/completions  close_tag=False len=1156  reasoning_content=None
A chat/completions  close_tag=False len=1347  reasoning_content=None
-> 0/5 contained '</think>'

B completions       close_tag=True  len=849
B completions       close_tag=True  len=887
B completions       close_tag=True  len=1034
B completions       close_tag=True  len=1132
B completions       close_tag=True  len=810
-> 5/5 contained '</think>'
```

`finish_reason` is `stop` in all ten samples, so this is not truncation. The
returned `content` in case A still contains the full deliberation followed by the
answer — nothing is dropped, but the two are now indistinguishable:

```
Here's a thinking process:

1.  **Understand the User's Request**: ...
   [~700 more characters of deliberation]

17 × 23 = **391**
```

#### Where it happens

`qwen3_xml` resolves to the combined engine in `vllm/parser/qwen3.py`, which owns
the reasoning phase as well as tool calls: it starts in `ParserState.REASONING`
and its `THINK_END` transition emits a `REASONING_END` event without re-emitting
the literal tag.

```python
# vllm/parser/qwen3.py
initial_state=ParserState.REASONING if thinking else ParserState.CONTENT,
...
(ParserState.REASONING, "THINK_END"): Transition(
    ParserState.CONTENT,
    (EventType.REASONING_END,),
),
# Absorb duplicate </think> — model may emit it after
# already transitioning to CONTENT; drop it silently.
(ParserState.CONTENT, "THINK_END"): Transition(
    ParserState.CONTENT,
    (),
),
```

That is correct behaviour when a reasoning parser is present to receive the
reasoning segment. When one is *not* configured, the segment has nowhere to go
and is folded back into `content` — minus its delimiter.

Note `Qwen3Parser.__init__` derives `thinking` from
`chat_template_kwargs.get("enable_thinking", True)` only — nothing consults
whether a reasoning parser is actually attached.

#### What the reasoning adapter does (the workaround)

Instantiating the adapters directly — CPU, no server — shows the reasoning path
is healthy, so this is purely about the asymmetric configuration:

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
from vllm.reasoning.qwen3_engine_reasoning_parser import Qwen3ParserReasoningAdapter

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B")
gen = "Let me work it out.\n17*20=340, 17*3=51, sum 391.\n</think>\n\n17 x 23 = **391**"
Qwen3ParserReasoningAdapter(tok).extract_reasoning(gen, request)
```

```
reasoning_content = 'Let me work it out.\n17*20=340, 17*3=51, sum 391.\n'
content           = '\n\n17 x 23 = **391**'
```

`extract_tool_calls` on a reply whose tool call follows `</think>` also returns
`tools_called=True`, so attaching the reasoning parser does **not** reintroduce
the failure mode of #39056 on this version — I could not reproduce that here.

Same check on the tool adapter shows the merge from the other side: for a reply
that deliberates and then calls a tool, the leftover content is
`'Thinking about it.'` — the reasoning, tag removed.

#### Expected behaviour

With a tool parser configured and no reasoning parser, one of:

1. leave `</think>` in `content` (i.e. the tool-call parser is transparent with
   respect to the reasoning phase), so clients can split as they could under the
   old split parsers; or
2. populate `reasoning_content` anyway, since the combined parser has in fact
   separated the two; or
3. warn, or refuse the configuration at startup, so the loss is not silent.

Any of these is fine; the current behaviour is the one option that loses
information without saying so.

#### Why this configuration exists at all

Deliberately, in our case. With the reasoning inline in `content`, every OpenAI
-compatible client replays the model's own deliberation as ordinary content;
`reasoning_content` is non-standard and most agent CLIs drop it on the floor. So
"tool parser, no reasoning parser" is not a misconfiguration to be talked out of
— it is the configuration that keeps thinking visible to clients that only speak
the standard schema.

#### Context: this is an edge of the unified-parser migration

The combined engine is the shape proposed in #32713, *[RFC]: Unified Parser for
reasoning, tool calling* — closed as not planned / stale, though the unified
parser landed. By my reading the RFC never discussed the asymmetric
configuration, which is exactly where the reasoning segment ends up with no
consumer and its delimiter removed. Under the old split parsers the tool parser
had no reasoning phase to own and the tag survived by construction.

#### Impact

We drive Qwen3.6-27B through a dozen different agent CLIs and reconstruct
trajectories from the HTTP traffic. Every one of those harnesses reports zero
thinking content on this stack, because they all split on `</think>`. It is a
labelling loss rather than a data loss, but it is unrecoverable downstream and
it is silent — nothing in the response indicates a boundary was removed.

#### Possibly related

These describe the opposite direction (content ending up in `reasoning`, or tool
calls trapped in reasoning) and are on 0.19.x, i.e. before the combined parser:

- #39056 — tool calls lost when XML markup is emitted inside `<think>`
  (`--reasoning-parser qwen3` + `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`)
- #35221 — reasoning-only output parsed as `content` (closed, PR #35230)
- #40816, #38894 — answer emitted in `reasoning`, `content` empty

#### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I have searched for similar existing issues and read the
  [troubleshooting docs](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/usage/troubleshooting.html).

items.title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash (glm5next) — recurring CUDA illegal memory access on 4xB200, surfacing in three unrelated kernels (KDA linear-attention, MHC TileLang, TRT-LLM fused MoE)
items.body:
### Your current environment

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash-x86_64-cu130` (`sha256:2e771fa615452282cc331eb418b3ef21636fce355bea0491fca89e6d362ab703`, published 2026-08-26 — the newest `glm53-flash` tag on Docker Hub)
- `vllm.__version__` = `0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187`
- tilelang 0.1.12
- 4x NVIDIA B200 (SM100), TP=4, driver healthy: 0 uncorrected ECC, no pending page retirement, no Xid, `Remapping Failure Occurred: No` on all 4 GPUs
- Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`)

Note this model is not upstream yet (#53906 is open), so this is filed against the day-0 image.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The engine dies with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` → `EngineDeadError`, repeatedly, under ordinary production chat traffic. Five crashes over ~6 hours, at 22 min / 10 min / 47 min / 2 h 34 min / 62 min of uptime. Before this the same box ran **15.5 h without a crash**, so it is load/state dependent rather than a startup or config error.

**The distinguishing detail: the fault surfaces in three completely unrelated kernel families, and different TP ranks of the same crash report different kernels.**

| Crash | Time (UTC) | Uptime | Faulting frame |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2026-08-28 22:48:48 | 22 min | `glm5next/nvidia/kda.py:581 _forward` → `flash_linear_attention/ops/kda.py:1576 chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` → `:1488 _fwd` → `ops/index.py:27 prepare_chunk_indices` |
| 2 | 2026-08-28 23:08:46 | 10 min | `glm5next/nvidia/model.py:558 hc_fused_post_pre` → `layers/mhc.py:409 forward_cuda` → `kernels/mhc/tilelang.py:635 mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang` → `tilelang/jit/kernel.py:202` |
| 3 | 2026-08-29 00:18:55 | 47 min | same as #2 (`mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang`) |
| 4 | 2026-08-29 02:58:08 | 2 h 34 min | **mixed per rank**: 3 ranks `mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang` / `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang` (TileLang, `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`); 1 rank `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` (`kda.py:581`, Triton) |
| 5 | 2026-08-29 05:04:08 | 62 min (PDL disabled — see below) | **mixed per rank**: TRT-LLM fused MoE `trtllm_fused_moe_dev_kernel.cu:991` on all 4 ranks; `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` (Triton) also reported |

Because the errors are asynchronous, we read these as *where the fault surfaced*, not where it originated — `prepare_chunk_indices` calls `.tolist()`, which forces the sync that reports crash #1. Two unrelated victims suggests a single upstream corrupter (most likely in the linear-attention/state path) that other kernels then trip over.

### Serve command

```
vllm serve /workspace/models/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --served-model-name glm-5.3-flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 524288 --max-num-seqs 1024 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.94 --enable-prefix-caching \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 --enable-prompt-tokens-details
```
`max_num_batched_tokens=16384` (default). No MTP, no LMCache, no `--mamba-cache-mode`.
Traffic is ordinary `/v1/chat/completions` (~95%) plus `/v1/responses` (~5%), 4–23 concurrent.

### What we ruled out

- **Hardware** — 0 ECC/Xid/page-retirement on all 4 GPUs.
- **Disk / JIT cache corruption** — 291 GB free.
- **Host RAM** — 48 of 1996 GB used.
- **A new client or changed workload** — same client IPs before and after the stable period.
- **`--mamba-cache-mode align`** — removed it (it is LMCache-only and LMCache was not running); crashed again at 47 min.
- **TileLang JIT-during-inference.** The JIT monitor does warn (`TileLang JIT compilation during inference: mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang`) and glm5next has **no mHC warmup module** — `model_executor/warmup/` covers DSv4, Kimi-K3, Qwen and MiniMax but not glm5next, so the DSv4 warmup work (#52941, #51802, #49707, #50178) does not cover this model. **But we correlated compile timestamps against all three crashes and found none nearby** — every compile happens in the first seconds after startup. So missing warmup is a real latency gap here, but it is not this crash.
- **`cu_seqlens` int32→int64 (`878631b60`, "normalize GDN sequence offsets")** — does not apply: that fix is in `fi_chunk_gated_delta_rule` (Qwen GDN + FlashInfer), and the glm5next KDA path is pure FLA Triton and never calls it. PR head's own `glm5next/nvidia/kda.py` has no such cast and `gdn_attn.py` remains int32.

### A failed workaround worth recording

Routing `MHCFusedPostPreOp.forward_cuda` to `self.forward_native(...)` — mirroring what `forward_hip` already does when `HAS_TILELANG_MHC` is false — **produces garbage output**, e.g.

```
', in inin fenslin green tit correct correctver in correctsenswald verververver that-n anglever thatv'
```

and runs ~6x slower. So on CUDA the torch decomposition in `MHCFusedPostPreOp.forward_native` does not appear to be numerically equivalent to `mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang`. That may be worth a separate look, given `forward_hip` relies on that same fallback for gfx942 (where TileLang MHC is already disabled for "incorrect results").

Also note `MHCFusedPostPreOp.enabled()` returns `True` unconditionally, so `-O.custom_ops=-mhc_fused_post_pre` cannot disable this op — there is no supported way to route around the TileLang kernel on CUDA.

### Code-review observation (mixed batches take the chunk path unpeeled)

`GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder` builds chunk metadata from a *prefill-only, rebased* `cu_seqlens`
and states the invariant explicitly (`gdn_attn.py`):

```python
# In a mixed non-spec batch, decodes are peeled off to the recurrent kernel (decode-first
# front slice), so build chunk metadata from the rebased prefill-only cu_seqlens; otherwise
# use the full non-spec one. _forward_core keys off the same condition, so they agree.
prefill_query_start_loc = non_spec_query_start_loc[num_decodes:] - num_decode_tokens
prefill_state_indices   = non_spec_state_indices_tensor[num_decodes:]
```

`Glm5NextKDA._forward` does **not** peel decodes. It branches `if num_prefills > 0: <chunk path>`
/ `elif num_decodes > 0: <recurrent path>`, so whenever a batch contains **both** decodes and
prefills, every non-spec token — including the 1-token decode sequences — goes through
`chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` with the **full, non-rebased** `cu_seqlens` and the full
`non_spec_state_indices_tensor`. `qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py`, which the builder was written
against, does peel them.

This is benign for the precomputed metadata itself: nothing in `glm5next/` reads
`chunk_indices`/`chunk_offsets`/`prefill_state_indices` (only `qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py` does), and
`chunk_kda_with_fused_gate_fwd` recomputes `prepare_chunk_indices(cu_seqlens, ...)` internally. So
the stale-metadata path is not the bug.

What we cannot rule out is the shape distribution: glm5next drives the chunked-prefill kernel with
batches containing many length-1 sequences interleaved with long prefills, which the builder's own
comment says should never reach that kernel. Is the unpeeled mixed batch intended for this model?

⚠️ To be clear about what this is NOT: we checked the base rate before reading anything into it.
Over 6,897 engine throughput samples on this box, prefill is active in **85.9%** of steps and
mixed batches (prefill AND decode both non-zero) are likewise **85.9%**. All four crashes occurred
during mixed batches, but at that base rate that is p ≈ 0.54 — no signal. Likewise both KDA
crashes landed in `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` (prefill) and neither in `fused_recurrent_kda`
(decode), but since glm5next takes the chunk path whenever `num_prefills > 0`, that kernel is live
in ~86% of steps versus ~14% for the recurrent one, so 2/2 is p ≈ 0.74 — also pure exposure.
**There is no prefill-vs-decode signal in our data.** The mixed-batch question above is raised on
the strength of the code divergence alone, not on any observed correlation.

(We also checked and ruled out a stale-`@tensor_cache` theory for `prepare_chunk_indices`: the
identity-keyed cache cannot go stale here because `input_batch.py` hands out
`input_buffers.query_start_loc[: num_reqs + 1]`, a fresh slice object each step.)

### Tested and falsified: PDL trigger-before-store in the mamba ops

Per PDL semantics, memory operations executed **after** `cudaTriggerProgrammaticLaunchCompletion`
are not guaranteed visible to a dependent grid past its `cudaGridDependencySynchronize`. The mamba
Triton ops fire the trigger at the **top of the kernel, before their loads and stores**:

```python
# gather_initial_states.py / scatter_states.py / causal_conv1d.py (launch_pdl=is_arch_support_pdl())
if launch_pdl:
    tl.extra.cuda.gdc_wait()
    tl.extra.cuda.gdc_launch_dependents()   # <-- trigger fired here
...
values = tl.load(...)                        # loads and stores happen AFTER the trigger
tl.store(...)
```

so a PDL-launched consumer can legally observe stale memory. (The MHC TileLang kernels do it
correctly — `T.pdl_sync()` at entry, `T.pdl_trigger()` after stores — but `mhc_pre_big_fuse`
reads its GEMM inputs immediately after `pdl_sync`, with the prenorm GEMM's trigger placement
inside the vendored library.) Since `is_arch_support_pdl()` is `major >= 9`, this code path is
live only on Hopper/Blackwell — consistent with a B200-only, intermittent, timing-dependent
fault whose reporters are simply the most frequently launched error-checking kernels (KDA chunk:
34/45 layers; MHC: every layer — matching the per-rank reporter mix with no phase signal). A related
latent defect: `_scatter_states_kernel` performs an unguarded `tl.store` at
`state_ptr + state_idx * stride`, with no NULL_BLOCK_ID check, where its decode-side counterpart
(`fused_recurrent.py`) explicitly guards `state_idx <= 0` on load and `> 0` on store.

**Tested: crash #5 occurred with `is_arch_support_pdl()` forced to `False`** (verified live in
the worker interpreter), at 62 minutes uptime, same `an illegal memory access`. Reporter this
time was the TRT-LLM fused MoE (`trtllm_fused_moe_dev_kernel.cu:991`, all 4 ranks) alongside KDA
on another rank — a third distinct reporting site, further confirming the fault is asynchronous
and upstream of every reporter. The trigger-before-store placement and the unguarded
`_scatter_states_kernel` store remain latent defects worth fixing, but they are not this bug.

### Structured output: present in all crash batches, but base-rate-neutral

All 3 crashes that produced a `dump_input` SchedulerOutput show
`has_structured_output_requests=true` with live xgrammar `json_object` requests — however we
then measured the base rate and **98.4% of this deployment's arrivals are structured**, so that
is exposure, not signal. One anomaly stands on its own: the only two
`backend_xgrammar.py:166 Failed to advance FSM ... tokens [154827]` errors in the log each
preceded a crash by 13–24 minutes; a grammar rejecting a token it should have masked to `-inf`
suggests the bitmask occasionally fails to apply — possibly the same corruption surfacing
non-fatally.

### Ask

Is there a known memory-safety issue in the glm5next KDA / mHC path on SM100? We have per-crash snapshots (full worker tracebacks, `nvidia-smi -q`, metrics, in-flight request shapes) and can run targeted instrumentation on the box — happy to attach anything useful.

items.body:

[pip3] torch_c_dlpack_ext==0.1.5
[pip3] torchaudio==2.11.0+cu130
[pip3] torchcodec==0.15.0+cu130
[pip3] torchvision==0.28.0+cu130
[pip3] transformers==5.15.0
[pip3] triton==3.7.1

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Description of the bug

Streaming tool calls (`stream: true`) on DeepSeek-V4-Pro with the `deepseek_v4` tool call parser leak raw DSML markup into tool call arguments. Non-streaming mode works correctly.

## Reproduction

### Hosted
```python
import json, requests

BASE = "http://<server>:8000/v1"
MODEL = "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro"

tools = [{
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get weather for a location",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "location": {"type": "string"},
                "date": {"type": "string"}
            },
            "required": ["location"]
        }
    }
}]

messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "What's the weather in Paris and Tokyo tomorrow?"}]

resp = requests.post(f"{BASE}/chat/completions", json={
    "model": MODEL,
    "messages": messages,
    "tools": tools,
    "tool_choice": "required",
    "stream": True,
}, stream=True, timeout=120)

for line in resp.iter_lines():
    if not line: continue
    line = line.decode("utf-8")
    if line.startswith("data: "):
        data = line[6:]
        if data == "[DONE]": break
        chunk = json.loads(data)
        delta = chunk["choices"][0].get("delta", {})
        if delta.get("tool_calls"):
            print(json.dumps(delta["tool_calls"]))
```
**Expected**: clean argument deltas like `{"location": "Paris"}`

**Actual**: DSML markup leaks into arguments:
```json
{"tool_calls": [{"index": 0, "function": {"arguments": "{\"location\": \""}}]}
{"tool_calls": [{"index": 0, "function": {"arguments": "Paris</\uff5cDSML\uff5cparameter"}}]}
{"tool_calls": [{"index": 0, "function": {"arguments": "\", \"date\": \""}}]}
```
### Regex-level reproduction (no model, GPU, or server required)

```python
import re, json

_DSML = "｜DSML｜"
_ESCAPED_DSML = re.escape(_DSML)

_PARAM_RE = re.compile(
    rf'<{_ESCAPED_DSML}parameter\s+name="([^"]+)"\s+string="(true|false)">'
    rf"(.*?)</{_ESCAPED_DSML}parameter>",
    re.DOTALL,
)
_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE = re.compile(
    rf'<{_ESCAPED_DSML}parameter\s+name="([^"]+)"\s+string="(true|false)">'
    rf"(.*)$",
    re.DOTALL,
)

def _dsml_arg_converter(raw_args, partial):
    params = {}
    last_end = 0
    for m in _PARAM_RE.finditer(raw_args):
        name, is_str, value = m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)
        params[name] = value if is_str == "true" else value
        last_end = m.end()
    if partial:
        pm = _PARTIAL_PARAM_RE.search(raw_args, last_end)
        if pm:
            params[pm.group(1)] = pm.group(3)
    return json.dumps(params, ensure_ascii=False)

# slot.args with a partial closing tag (missing final >)
raw = "<｜DSML｜parameter name=\"location\" string=\"true\">Paris</｜DSML｜parameter"
print(_dsml_arg_converter(raw, partial=True))
# Output: {"location": "Paris</｜DSML｜parameter"}
# Expected: {"location": "Paris"}
```
## Possible root cause

PR #45877 (commit `fb5291b35b`, July 3 2026) ported DeepSeek V4 from the hand-written `DeepSeekV32ToolParser` to the generic `StreamingParserEngine` framework. The new code introduced `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE` with `(.*)$` to capture in-progress parameter values during streaming.

## Impact

- `stream: true` with `tool_choice: required`: DSML markup leaks into argument JSON
- `stream: true` with `tool_choice: auto`: tool calls emitted with empty `{}` arguments (no arg deltas streamed)
- `stream: false`: works correctly (unaffected)
- Agent harnesses (e.g. opencode, Claude Code) that use streaming mode fail to execute tool calls

## Proposed fix

Change `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE` to use a negative lookahead that stops at DSML tag prefixes instead of greedily capturing everything:

```python
_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE = re.compile(
    rf'<{_ESCAPED_DSML}parameter\s+name="([^"]+)"\s+string="(true|false)">'
    rf"((?:(?!</?{_ESCAPED_DSML}).)*)",
    re.DOTALL,
)
```

## Related issues
- #40800 (closed), but the parser has changed since then

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Perf]: DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 on 4xH800: v0.28.0 needs ~4 GiB/GPU more non-KV memory than v0.26.0; my earlier TTFT-regression claim was caused by VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 on my side (retracted)
items.body:
> ## ⚠️ Correction 2026-09-02 — the TTFT/throughput regression reported below was caused by my own configuration, not by vLLM
>
> All my v0.28.0 runs had `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` (set to work around an OOM at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`). For `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`, which has no `@support_torch_compile`, the breakable CUDA graph **is the only piecewise-graph path** (as the comment in `config/vllm.py` says), so `=0` made every prefill-containing step run fully eager. With the default (`=1`) and `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`, **v0.28.0 is faster than v0.26.0 on every arm** (TTFT 22/32/41 ms vs 49/58/68 ms at conc 1/8/32; conc-32 throughput +35%). Full data and profiler evidence in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54677#issuecomment-5504401811). What remains real: v0.28.0 needs ~4 GiB/GPU more non-KV memory than v0.26.0 on this model, which is why 0.92 OOMed for us. I am sorry for the noise; maintainers may retitle/close as they see fit.

> **Baseline figures corrected 2026-09-01** — the v0.26 conc=8 / conc=32 TTFT numbers first posted here (183 ms / 330 ms) were misquoted from a different run. Re-derived from the baseline CSV, they are **57 ms / 69 ms**, which makes the regression larger than originally stated (up to ~24× at conc=32), not smaller. All 0.28 figures are unchanged.

### Summary

Serving **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731** on 4×H800 (SM90, TP4), upgrading **v0.26.0 → v0.28.0** improves decode throughput (+8–21%) but regresses **first-token latency ~6–20×**. There appears to be a **constant ~1s/request prefill overhead** in 0.28 that exists even for ~16-token prompts at concurrency 1, persists in steady state (it is the *median* over hundreds of post-warmup requests, not a first-touch/compile artifact), and compounds into severe admission queueing at moderate concurrency. We swept every knob we could find (details below) and could not recover 0.26-class TTFT.

### Environment

- 4×H800 80GB (SM90), single node, TP=4
- Driver 580.173.02 / CUDA 13.0
- `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0` official image (cu13 flavor), `--ipc=host --network host`
- Baseline: v0.26.0 (pip venv, torch cu129) on the same node, same weights, same flags
- Model: local `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (fp8), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, model-native max len (1M)
- Serve flags (both versions): `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-prompt-tokens-details` (variations noted per row)
- Load generator: async OpenAI-compat client, ~16-token prompts, 200–400 token outputs, temperature 0, concurrency 1 / 8 / 32
- Test order per config: one ~22k-token warmup request first, then single, then conc=8 (~80+ requests), then conc=32 (~100–300 requests) — so the conc=32 medians are measured on an engine that has already served 100+ requests
- All 0.28 runs use `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`. With the auto-enabled default (=1, which logs that it disables the torch.compile pipeline) we instead hit CUDA OOM: at init with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`, or on the first ~22k-token prefill with 0.90. This matches the throughput findings in #49370, so the whole sweep was done with `=0`.

### Numbers (TTFT p50 per request; decode tok/s per stream)

| Config | single TTFT | conc=8 TTFT | conc=32 TTFT | conc=32 decode/stream |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **v0.26.0** (MRV1, 8192, util 0.90) | **48 ms** | **57 ms** | **69 ms** | 58.8 |
| v0.28.0, 8192, util 0.90, +kv-offloading 200GB | 681 ms | 1013 ms | **48.1 s** | (99.1, inflated by queueing) |
| v0.28.0, 8192, util 0.90 | n/a | 1188 ms | 7.10 s | 76.8 |
| v0.28.0, **16384**, util 0.85 (new default budget) | n/a | 1093 ms | **1.81 s** (best) | 63.4 |
| v0.28.0, MRV1 forced (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, cudagraph_mode FULL_DECODE_ONLY, 8192, 0.90) | n/a | 1172 ms | 2.34 s | 56.7 |
| v0.28.0, 16384, 0.85, `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB=4096` | n/a | 1254 ms | 2.16 s | 56.5 |
| v0.28.0, 16384, 0.85, `VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` | n/a | 981 ms | **49.3 s** | **15.4 (collapse)** |
| v0.28.0, MRV1 forced + 16384 + 0.85 | — | — | — | engine core init failure |

Observations:

1. **A constant ~1s/request first-token cost is present in every 0.28 config**, including single-stream with ~16-token prompts (681 ms vs 48 ms on 0.26 — 14×). It is steady-state: conc=8 p50 sits at 1.0–1.2 s in *every* configuration across ~80 post-warmup requests (0.26 does 57 ms), and the single-stream case shows all three sequential requests equally slow, not just the first. It is also not a long-prompt chunking effect: raising `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` 512→4096 changed nothing, and the tiny-prompt case shows the overhead too.
2. Raising `--max-num-batched-tokens` to the new 16384 default (#51726) recovers most of the *queueing* (48 s → 1.8 s at conc=32) but the per-request floor remains ~1 s.
3. Forcing Model Runner V1 (allowed per #51768 with non-piecewise graphs) improves conc=32 TTFT ~3× vs MRV2 at the same flags (7.1 s → 2.3 s), but is still ~7× off 0.26, and fails engine-core init when combined with 16384 + util 0.85.
4. The default sparse backend (FlashMLA family) is the better of the two on SM90: forcing `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` collapses conc=32 decode to 15 tok/s with ~49 s TTFT.
5. Decode throughput is genuinely better on 0.28 in clean configs (single 149.8 → 174.9, conc=8 100.6 → 122.3, conc=32 58.6 → 63.4 tok/s) — the regression is specific to the prefill/first-token path.
6. KV offloading (`--kv-offloading-size 200`) works functionally on 0.28 (≈258 GB written through, no crashes — thanks for the post-0.26 fixes), but under load it amplifies the TTFT problem (48 s at conc=32), presumably from transfer contention.

### Suspicion

The per-request floor smells like the new sparse MLA prefill path that became the default for this model in 0.27/0.28. Possibly related: #54179 and #52339 (FlashMLA sparse prefill assertions on H20 — same kernel family, adjacent SM90 hardware), and #51430/#52401 (eager cudagraph region reshuffling for this model, which is also what forces MRV2 by default per #51768).

### Questions

1. Is a ~0.7–1.2 s per-request first-token floor for DSV4 on SM90 known/expected on 0.28, or a regression worth bisecting?
2. Is there a supported way to select the 0.26-era prefill path for this model on 0.28+, to keep the decode gains without the TTFT floor?

Happy to run additional experiments or bisect specific PRs on this hardware — the node and the harness that produced the table are still available.

items.title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash — ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoints emit invalid UTF-8 byte tokens on SM120, while a compressed-tensors NVFP4 of the same model is clean
items.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```text
GPUs:     4x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GiB, SM120), PCIe, no NVLink
Image:    cstechdev/vllm:glm53-flash-nope-sm120-cu130-20260826-r1
          (a NoPE sparse-MLA overlay on vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash;
           github.com/chriswritescode-dev/glm-5.3-flash-sm120)
vLLM:     0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187
Model:    GLM-5.3-Flash (glm5_next), TP4
KV:       fp8_ds_mla (the only layout the SM120 sparse-MLA impl accepts)
MoE:      --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"marlin","enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}'
Other:    MTP off, --block-size auto (lands on 1792), --enable-prefix-caching
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Two ModelOpt-produced NVFP4 conversions of GLM-5.3-Flash emit **invalid UTF-8 byte-token
sequences** during generation on SM120. A compressed-tensors NVFP4 conversion of the *same*
model, served from the same image with the same kernel, KV layout, parallelism and sampling
settings, is clean. Only the checkpoint changes between these rows.

The failure is quiet: the server returns HTTP 200, throughput looks normal, English text is
mostly fine, and short prompts read correctly. It shows up as U+FFFD inside multi-byte
(here: Korean) text, which is easy to mistake for a rendering or client problem.

#### Result

Six generations per row — 3 at `temperature=0.0`, 3 at `0.7`, identical Korean prompt,
`max_tokens=4096`. The count is U+FFFD characters across `content` + `reasoning`.

| checkpoint | quant format | U+FFFD / 6 runs | degenerate loops |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `LibertAIDAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` | modelopt NVFP4 | **86** | 0/6 |
| `LibertAIDAI/...` @ rev `cf5434c00b` (43-entry ignore list) | modelopt NVFP4 | **62** | 1/6 |
| `dealignai/GLM-5.3-Flash-UNCENSORED-NVFP4` | modelopt NVFP4 | **94** | 0/6 |
| `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` | compressed-tensors NVFP4 | **0** | 0/6 |

Sample from a `temperature=0` generation on the LibertAI checkpoint — `퍼셉트론`
(“perceptron”) loses its middle syllable:

```
프랭크 로젠블랫(Frank Rosenblatt)의 퍼<?>트론(Perceptron, 1957)
```

#### This is not a detokenizer artifact

Requesting `return_token_ids: true` and decoding the returned ids offline with the
checkpoint's own tokenizer reproduces the same U+FFFD count as the API text (5 and 5 on the
sampled request), so the emitted token ids themselves do not form valid UTF-8. Byte-token
continuations are near-deterministic, so producing an invalid continuation under greedy
decoding points at the logits rather than at decoding.

#### Ruled out

Each of these was varied independently with everything else held fixed:

- **Context length** — a Korean prompt answered correctly at 62, 25 772, 103 040, 412 112 and
  1 030 162 prompt tokens, with both Korean and English filler. Corruption appears at
  **zero context** too, so it is not the sparse-MLA/long-context path.
- **Sampling** — present at `temperature=0.0`.
- **MTP** — `num_speculative_tokens` 5 and 0 behave the same.
- **PDL** — patching `CudaPlatformBase.is_arch_support_pdl` to exclude SM12x changes nothing.
- **Abliteration** — the guardrail-removed `dealignai` build and its un-abliterated
  `LibertAIDAI` sibling score the same (94 vs 86).
- **`quantization_config.ignore` completeness** — our LibertAI copy predated commit
  `cf5434c00b`, which grew the ignore list from 32 to 43 entries (fused attention
  projections, `q/k/v/qkv_conv1d`, `o_norm`, `visual.*`). Updating `config.json` to that
  revision — weights untouched — left corruption in place (86 → 62, within the run-to-run
  spread of 7–22 per generation).

#### Open question

The two checkpoint families differ in **loader path**, not only in file format: modelopt vs
compressed-tensors. So this data cannot distinguish

- (A) the two ModelOpt conversions carry damaged weights, from
- (B) vLLM's ModelOpt NVFP4 path is wrong here while the compressed-tensors NVFP4 path is
  correct.

If (B), every ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint is affected, not just this model. Someone able to
compare the two loaders' dequantized weights for the same tensor would settle it quickly;
we do not have a reference to diff against.

#### Side observation: NvFp4 MoE backend availability on SM120

While isolating the above, with the checkpoint held fixed:

| `moe_backend` | result on SM120 |
|---|---|
| `flashinfer_trtllm` | rejected — `kernel does not support current device cuda` |
| `flashinfer_cutedsl` | rejected — same |
| `flashinfer_cutlass` | **6/6 runs collapse into a repeated single token** (`locklocklock…`) |
| `cutlass` (VLLM_CUTLASS) | **6/6 collapse**, no `content` produced at all |
| `emulation` | collapses — 49 129 chars of `</arg_value>` repeats, 0 % Hangul |
| `marlin` | the only usable path |

The two CUTLASS failures line up with sgl-project/sglang#18954 (“NVFP4 models produce NaN
outputs on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120)”), which was closed on the FlashInfer side; this is
the same symptom reached through vLLM, and it reproduces on vLLM's own CUTLASS path as well.
That `emulation` also collapses is the part we cannot explain — a dequantizing reference path
should be the safe fallback.

#### Reproduction

```bash
docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host --shm-size 32g -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /data/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4:/model:ro \
  cstechdev/vllm:glm53-flash-nope-sm120-cu130-20260826-r1 /model \
  --served-model-name GLM-5.3-Flash --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-model-len 131072 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"marlin","enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --enable-prefix-caching --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45
```

Then ask for a long answer in a language with multi-byte characters and count U+FFFD:

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model":"GLM-5.3-Flash","temperature":0,"max_tokens":4096,
  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"인공지능의 역사를 1950년대부터 현재까지 시대별로 나누어 한국어로 자세히 설명해 주세요."}]
}' | python3 -c 'import json,sys; m=json.load(sys.stdin)["choices"][0]["message"]; t=(m.get("content") or "")+(m.get("reasoning") or ""); print("U+FFFD:", t.count("�"))'
```

Swapping `/model` to `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` with everything else identical returns 0.

### 🐛 Describe the bug


When using the Responses API (`/v1/responses`) with streaming enabled and a non-harmony model that uses XML-based tool calls (e.g. Qwen3.5), tool call content is emitted as `response.output_text.delta` events containing raw XML instead of proper `response.function_call_arguments.delta` / `response.function_call_arguments.done` events.

The non-streaming Responses API, Chat Completions streaming, and Chat Completions non-streaming all work correctly — only Responses API streaming is affected.

### Root Cause

In `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py`, `_process_simple_streaming_events` has two issues:

1. **`reasoning_parser` and `tool_parser` are mutually exclusive in the `if/elif` chain.** When a model has both a reasoning parser (e.g. `<think>` tags) and a tool parser, the `elif tool_parser:` branch is never reached because `if reasoning_parser:` always takes priority. After reasoning ends, subsequent tokens (including `<tool_call>` XML) fall through as plain content.

2. **No tool call event emission.** Even if the tool parser were reached, there was no code to convert `DeltaMessage.tool_calls` into `ResponseFunctionCallArgumentsDeltaEvent` / `ResponseFunctionCallArgumentsDoneEvent`. The original code had `# todo(kebe7jun) tool call support`.

### Reproduce

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="dummy")

# Streaming Responses API with tool calls
with client.responses.create(
    model="Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B",  # or any non-harmony model with tool call support
    input="What's the weather in Boston today?",
    tools=[{
        "type": "function",
        "name": "get_current_weather",
        "description": "Get the current weather in a given location",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "location": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "The city and state, e.g. San Francisco, CA"
                },
                "unit": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"]
                }
            },
            "required": ["location", "unit"]
        }
    }],
    stream=True,
) as stream:
    for event in stream:
        print(event)
```

Server started with:
```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder
```

### Actual behavior

Tool call XML leaks into text delta events:

```
response.output_text.delta  → "<tool_call>"
response.output_text.delta  → "\n<function=get_current_weather>"
response.output_text.delta  → "\n<parameter=location>"
response.output_text.delta  → "Boston, MA"
...
response.output_text.done   → "\n\n<tool_call>\n<function=get_current_weather>\n<parameter=location>\nBoston, MA\n</parameter>\n<parameter=unit>\nfahrenheit\n</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>"
```

### Expected behavior

Proper function call events (matching OpenAI's Responses API behavior):

```
response.output_item.added              → {type: "function_call", name: "get_current_weather", status: "in_progress"}
response.function_call_arguments.delta  → "{"
response.function_call_arguments.delta  → '"location": "Boston, MA"'
response.function_call_arguments.delta  → ', "unit": "fahrenheit"'
response.function_call_arguments.delta  → "}"
response.function_call_arguments.done   → '{"location": "Boston, MA", "unit": "fahrenheit"}'
response.output_item.done               → {type: "function_call", arguments: '{"location": "Boston, MA", "unit": "fahrenheit"}'}
```

### Related

- #29725
- #26874 (fixed non-streaming path only)

### Fix

I have a fix at https://github.com/herve-ves/vllm/tree/fix/responses-streaming-tool-call — happy to open a PR if desired.

The fix modifies `_process_simple_streaming_events` to:
1. Handle both reasoning and tool calls (reasoning first, then tool calls after `is_reasoning_end()`, matching Chat Completions behavior)
2. Emit `ResponseFunctionCallArgumentsDeltaEvent` / `ResponseFunctionCallArgumentsDoneEvent` via existing `emit_function_call_delta_events` / `emit_function_call_done_events` helpers
3. Properly close message output items before function call events when content precedes tool calls
4. Sync `tool_streaming_state.current_output_index` with the main output index


### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
